sources.title: Save and Grow: Cassava
sources.publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.notes: The guide says cassava is usually planted in southern Nigeria in March-April at the onset of rains. The source does not specify Akwa Ibom LGAs or a variety-specific calendar.

sources.title: Variability in Length of Rainy Season for Selected Crops Production in Coastal and Upland Areas of Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria
sources.publisher: International Journal of Agriculture, Environment and Bioresearch
sources.geographicScope: Study sites include coastal Eket and Oron and upland Uyo and Ikot Ekpene; rainfall observations cover 1989-2018
sources.notes: The study reports that only upland areas in its sample supported sustainable yam and cassava production. It does not give a cassava planting-month calendar. It is not an assessment of every farm or of Ikot Abasi.

locations.reviewNote: The local study treats Eket as a coastal site and does not support sustainable yam or cassava production in its coastal/upland comparison. It gives no planting window for other crops. No crop windows are entered for Eket. This is not a farm-level soil assessment.
The reviewed crop-timing sources do not directly cover Ikot Abasi. No planting window is entered for this LGA. The existing broad-zone assignment is marked for local review.

A broad FAO guide gives March-April as the usual southern Nigeria cassava planting period, tied to the onset of rains. An Akwa Ibom study sampled Ikot Ekpene as an upland site and reports upland suitability for sustainable cassava production. This is reviewed regional guidance, not farm-specific advice; a qualified agronomist has not approved it.
